title: Special Edition: The Shield Hero’s Valentine’s Day Part 8
text: Chocolate Monster… What an amazing choice of name. I wonder if this is the limited-time monster everyone’s been talking about.
“Hurry up and call the Sword Hero!”
“Ooh!”
…So this is where Ren is doing his thing.
“Raphtalia, and… you.”
“Yes.”
“Kue.”

I pointed at the Chocolate Monster toward Raphtalia and Chick (even though “-chan” is part of her name, I don’t want to call her that). Raphtalia and Chick immediately understood my intention and scattered the Chocolate Monster. It wasn’t very strong, was it? Raphtalia and Chick took down the Chocolate Monster that had appeared with a single blow.
“Ah, it’s the Shield Hero.”
“Lord Iwatani? It’s rare to run into you here.”
“Isn’t that Naofumi?”

Just as they defeated the monsters, Ren arrived. And look—the female knight and Taniko are right behind him, too. I thought they kept their distance, but it turns out they’re actually hanging out together after all.
By the way, Gaelion isn’t here. What the hell is he up to? I’m pretty sure he was in the village. I remember seeing him before I left.
“That’s unusual. I never thought I’d see you guys hanging out with Ren.”
“Huh?”
“Huh?”

Huh? These two… they’re hanging out together pretty often, aren’t they…? What’s with all the “annoying” and “I’m not interested in romance” nonsense? No matter what they say, they’re still together, aren’t they? These tsundere types.
“Nah, never mind.”
But it’s a hassle to pry that out of them. More importantly, I’m not interested in their love lives. If they want to do it, they can just go ahead and do it on their own.
“…Are they fighting around here?”
“No, they’re active over a wide area, not just this region.”
“Huh. For that, you got here pretty fast.”
“The boss monster that appeared during the Valentine’s Day event fled to this area. Apparently, if we find and defeat it, things will calm down to some extent…”

So they’re dealing with a hassle. Is there actually a boss or something? Is this some kind of turf war? Since dragons are the kings of monsters, calling in Gaelion or someone like that would probably solve it…

No, wait—this smell. I doubt even a nose could pick it up. Plus, since it’s basically like chocolate moving around, it probably isn’t a living monster. I’d say it’s an inanimate monster, like a balloon. If that’s the case, it might be tricky.
“So, was that one from earlier the boss?”
“No, it wasn’t.”
“Is that so? Well, we took it down pretty easily, though.”
“Yeah, there are a few other types, but the boss is a fast runner…”
To actually outrun Ren, the Sword Hero… isn’t that pretty impressive? Yeah, Ren seems to have his hands full. I can’t handle this kind of monster-hunting law enforcement, so I can’t help out, though.
“An acquaintance of the Sword Hero… and always looking so sullen… Could it be the Shield Hero!?”

What kind of impression is that, you jerk! When I glared at Ren, he shook his head. Apparently, the rumor didn’t come from him. I mean, is that even a description of me—not an insult!? The moment the chocolate farmers found out who we really were, they prostrated themselves and bowed their heads.
“Thank you so much! Thanks to your heroic efforts, we’ve been able to keep our business going.”
“Cut it out. We’re here to maintain public order. Everyone, please get back to work. Right, Naofumi?”
“…Yeah, you’re right.”

I caught myself thinking that if I used the Shield Hero’s authority, I could probably buy up all their chocolate at a bargain price. Ren’s reaction was the right one, though… If I don’t rein myself in, I’ll get consumed by the Cursed Shield again. I forgot to explain this earlier, but there’s a major reason why I was consumed by the Cursed Shield in the past.

There’s something like a hidden stat called “Karma.” This is what judges whether a Hero is committing evil deeds or good deeds. It’s an element that becomes visible once you reach a certain level of strength and possess specific weapons. It seems that if this Karma surpasses a certain threshold, the Cursed Shield appears.

Of course, it’s not just your weapons that are judged—it’s your own heart as well—but the dynamics of how good and evil deeds affect your Karma are quite complex. Making a donation doesn’t automatically count as a good deed, and committing a misdeed doesn’t automatically count as an evil one. The correct answer is that if you do something that earns people’s respect and produces results, it can be a good deed… or it can be an evil one.

The reason I was consumed by the Cursed Shield in the past was because I was a money-grubbing miser and because of the Bio-Plant—I was trying to use it to solve every problem. Modifying plants when upgrading the Bio-Plant has a significant impact on your karma. Of course, since I was manufacturing things that were useful for daily life, my karma didn’t increase drastically.

But the point is, my past misdeeds and the way I treated the villagers all piled up, and that’s why I ended up cursed. Because of that, I act while being somewhat mindful of my karma. If I commit a misdeed but it ultimately benefits people, I get the same karma points as if I’d done a good deed. Things like secretly taking down unscrupulous merchants don’t seem to affect my karma either positively or negatively. Even if I have secret ties with a Robin Hood-type figure, there isn’t much change in my karma either way.

Right now, my karma is heavily tilted toward the good side. That’s thanks to my great feat of saving the world. Getting back to the point, since I’m the hero who saved the world, if I were to threaten him to sell it for practically nothing, my karma would definitely go into the negative. Plus, given the amount of money involved, it might drop quite a bit. It’s not worth taking that kind of risk.
“Well, I’ve got stuff to do, so I’m heading out. Good luck with your training, Ren.”
“Oh, actually, I wanted to talk to Naofumi about that.”
“What is it?”
“Wyndia says she wants to investigate the Chocolate Monster… It might end up being about money, which Naofumi likes.”
“It’s not like I actually like money or anything…”

It’s become a habit by now, and even if I say it’s to raise funds for reconstruction, I don’t think anyone would interpret it charitably. It all started because you guys—the other heroes, the Bitches, and that bunch of Trash—got me into financial trouble in the first place. It just became a habit, and making money is just a hobby now.
Still, analyzing a limited-time monster, huh? If it goes well, it could definitely lead to something interesting. Since Taniko loves monsters, it’s actually a pretty good angle.
“That old hag got a job at the village, right? So I’m the one who has to look into it… plus, there’s the question of why the chocolate is moving around only during this time of year.”
“Hmm…”

Taniko’s curiosity is understandable. Even if we just brush it off as “it’s a monster,” the fact that sludge-like chocolate is moving around is a mystery that never ends. And on top of that, it only appears for a limited time… I wonder what kind of mechanism is behind it? Apparently, there were Christmas-limited monsters too—I wonder if there are other types as well.

If we could tame them successfully, we might be able to harvest chocolate on a regular basis. We’ve already started stocking up on a fair number of those production-type monsters in our monster stable, and if it works out, it could certainly be a money-maker. Come to think of it, if these are the artificial monsters created by past heroes… well, that would explain everything, which is kind of scary. Judging by the vibe, they might fall into a category like “mutants” or something like that.

A plausible explanation might be that it’s the anger of a chocolate tree manifested in physical form… or that it emerged from contaminated soil? Come to think of it, are the carcasses of these chocolate monsters even edible? I wouldn’t want to eat them, but if they were actually mixed into the chocolate sold at the market, that would be mentally tough to handle.
“Taming that monster… is it even possible to tame it?”
“It was possible in the game… but this is different, right?”

Well, in games and such, taming mostly involves using items to capture them, but in this world, it seems like you have to find things like eggs or something along those lines. Couldn’t we just force it to obey using the intimidation of a Gaelion or something?
“Can’t we reason with it?”
“Nope. Unlike Balloons or Egggugs, which have a tiny bit of free will… this one’s just too frenzied to listen.”
“So they only show up for a limited-time event, and on top of that, they’re so worked up they won’t listen…”
“Yeah.”
That’s a tough problem. Just as I was lost in thought, the female knight stepped forward.
“Lord Iwatani, what brings you here?”
“You should know why I’m here, right? To buy chocolate.”
“I see. I thought for sure it was some kind of secret meeting.”
“Why the hell do I have to hold a meeting in a chocolate-smelling backwater like this!”
Lately, the female knight has been showing an extraordinary interest in my misdeeds. Not to stop me, but to learn from them.

“You’ve really hit rock bottom, female knight!” It’s easy to mock her, but her enthusiasm for learning about my misdeeds knows no bounds. She even said she wanted to attend the Righteous Thieves Guild’s meeting, so it was a real pain to shake her off. In eroge, female knights often end up turning to the dark side—it’s a pretty common trope—but with her, it’s somehow different.
“Sword Hero… Let’s hurry, shall we?”
“Yeah, we’ve got to take down the boss soon or the damage will keep piling up.”
“Can’t we just capture him alive?”
“It’s a favor for Wyndia, after all. I’ll do my best.”
“That’s true. If we capture him alive and study him, we might be able to start a new business just like Lord Iwatani did.”

Ren, Taniko, and the female knight carried on their conversation with amazing ease. These guys are actually pretty close, aren’t they? They’re just childhood friends who can’t bring themselves to admit it.
“Well then, Lord Iwatani, I’m not giving up. I’m going to steal your skills!”

With the female knight blabbering on like that, Ren and the others eventually headed back to work. Female knight, what on earth are you trying to do? Learn how to run a fiefdom by studying the ways of villains? Before anything else, you need to learn how to tell right from wrong!
With that, I parted ways with Ren and headed toward the chocolate farm.
